UNITY-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION (documented at length in the file's own class header): _skinBelt/_rideOne/_skinXform's math drops the JS's bodyInv/bindMatrix/bindMatrixInverse juggling (foot.js:1598-1600, 1691-1692, 1830-1834), which exists ONLY to work around three.js's SkinnedMesh.bindMatrixInverse being a live, per-frame-recomputed property that can go stale mid-frame (this project's own documented 'mid-frame bindMatrixInverse' bug class). Unity's Mesh.bindposes is fixed import-time data and a SkinnedMeshRenderer's own Transform plays no part in its skin computation at all, so inverting the blended bone matrix directly is the complete, always-correct solve -- a reasoned adaptation to a different engine contract, not a shortcut, and flagged as the single highest-risk piece of this file to have gotten subtly wrong. Built a brute-force Moller-Trumbore ray/triangle raycaster (FootBelt.Hull) as Unity's substitute for three.js's BVH-backed Raycaster.intersectObject, since Unity has no built-in 'raycast this loose vertex/index buffer' primitive; this is new code with no JS line of its own, used wherever the JS calls `ray.intersectObject(hull, false)[0]`.
